lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: why exponential growth eventually exceeds polynomial growth
lessonRef.title: Targeted correction: why exponential growth eventually exceeds polynomial growth

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

steps: It is the multiplier per year.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (4, 3) and (7, 0). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 2, 4, 6, 8. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 2.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 2.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.

items.prompt: A population of 900 grows by 7% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 7 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 31 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: A stays ahead permanently because 31 is larger than 3.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 2500(0.96)^t, with t in years. What does 0.96 represent?
choices: the total value lost over the asset's life
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.96, meaning a 4% annual loss
the value of the asset when it was new, $2500

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (5, -18) and (9, -26). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 11, 16, 21, 26. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 5.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 5.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.

items.prompt: A population of 4000 grows by 11% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 5 years, to the nearest whole number.
